newsitem.title: UK: QE II set for world cruise after refit.
newsitem.headline: QE II set for world cruise after refit.

text.p: The Queen Elizabeth II has completed a 12 million pound ($20 million) refit and will begin a 30th birthday world cruise in the second week of January, a spokesman for the luxury liner said on Wednesday.
The cruise will take the ship to the Caribbean, Mexico, Hawaii, Fiji, New Zealand, Australia, Japan, Hong Kong, India, the Middle East and the Mediterranean.

The Queen Elizabeth II, operated by Cunard Line Ltd, a subsidiary of Norwegian shipbuilding group Kvaerner ASA, will then return to its home port of Southampton in April to start a programme of Atlantic crossings and shorter European cruises.
The liner's reputation is still recovering from a disastrous Christmas cruise in to New York 1994 after an earlier refit that was not completed before the ship set sail.
That voyage cost Cunard 7.5 million pounds in compensation paid to passengers who complained of "exploding toilets", foul smells from plumbing and debris filling the ship's passageways.
The Queen Elizabeth II was launched on Scotland's river Clyde in 1967. Since then the ship has travelled more than four million miles and carried almost two million passengers.
